messages:
lena: Quick check — rolling out tenant-scoped telemetry flag (telemetry_v2) for enterprise customers. Need consensus on allowlist semantics + contract gating + VIP handling. We're planning: default OFF, allowlist by account id, contract-level override for signed ent plans, VIP accounts auto-opt-in with manual opt-out. Any missing guardrails? (cc @samir @jess)

samir: sounds reasonable. couple asks: 1) how do we detect contract-level entitlement? contract_id in /account/profile? 2) rollback plan? 3) monitoring hooks per tenant

jess: agree. implement as layered rules: explicit allowlist -> contract entitlement -> vip auto -> global default. Also require an expiry TTL on manual allow entries.

samir: +1 for TTL. also add rate-limit for telemetry ingestion per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors. consider soft-fail: if flag system times out, default to customer's current behaviour (usually OFF)

maria: for VIP handling: maintain a dedicated VIP list in secrets manager (not in feature flag) so ops can toggle quickly without code deploy. ops-bot can watch that file.

lena: noting: can we express the contract-level rule in feature flags? example rule:
```
- rule: contract_entitled
  if: account.contract_tier in ["enterprise", "enterprise_plus"]
  action: enable
```
If not, we'll enforce in application layer.

jess: LD can do targeting by custom attribute (contract_tier). if attributes are messy, prefer app-layer check + tag event for audit.

samir: Monitoring: add per-tenant counter (telemetry_v2_events) and a % change alert vs baseline; also a "ctr" for error rate. set a canary audience = 2% of accounts + all VIPs + 5 contracted accounts.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to staging in 15m, prod canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC if no showstoppers :rocket:

lena: I'll update the rollout doc with layered rules, TTL, VIP secret toggle, and canary audience. Will post PR for review shortly. thanks :thumbsup:
